independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: The span opens at Psalm 144's own parent boundary and closes cleanly at the 144.4|144.5 seam. Re-derived from verse_map_web/oshb: vv1-4 hold no imperative and no addressee change (v1 is a berakah formula addressed to Yahweh, v2 an appositive epithet chain, v3 a rhetorical question to Yahweh, v4 a gnomic simile), while v5 opens with an imperative (matching the imperative pattern that also reopens at v11) - the seam the row draws is the strongest tier-1 boundary in the span. The rejected 1-2/3-4 split is reasonably set aside on the same no-addressee/no-mode-change ground. The MT 144:1 two-paseq claim (single-witness, seg-layer) is confirmed against pmarks_Ps.json (paseq[Ps.144.1]=2) and correctly held to corroboration only, never a driver. The Ps 18 echo disclosures (18:2 rock/fortress/deliverer/shield/high-tower epithet catalog; 18:34 teaches-my-hands-to-war line) are content-accurate against verse_map_web and are correctly typed as a disclosed cross-psalm echo, not a merge signal - 144 keeps its own parent. The web:Ps.144.0 = oshb:Ps.144.1 opening citation matches web_mt_offset_map.json's identity ruling for 144 (web_verses=15, mt_verses=15, rule=identity) and the owner-mandated titled-opening-row form. All Hebrew quotes in this row collate at byte tier against verse_map_oshb (collate.py batch run). No defect found.

Span 5-8 is an unbroken imperative-and-petition unit: vv5-6 run a theophany imperative series (part/come down, touch; throw, scatter, send, rout), v7 turns to direct rescue petition, v8 closes on the foreigners' deceit - no addressee change anywhere in the span. The seam at 8|9 is well-grounded: v9 shifts to a first-person cohortative vow, a genuine mode change the row correctly cites as the reason a fresh row opens there, and correctly notes as unswept (imperative/mood claims sit outside the staged morphology layer and are argued from bytes plus both witnesses' renderings here, not from sweep.py). The Ps 18 storm-theophany parallel (18:9 heavens bowed and came down; 18:14 arrows sent out and scattered, routed with lightning; 18:16 many waters) is content-accurate against verse_map_web and correctly disclosed as texture, not a driver. All Hebrew quotes in this row collate at byte tier. No defect found.

Span 9-11 groups the new-song vow (9), the divine king-maker description (10), and a near-repeat of the 7-8 rescue plea (11) under one parent-consistent strophe, closing at 11|12 where a purpose clause opens the prosperity vision - the overall row grouping is defensible and the tiling is exact. The v8/v11-tail deceit clause is independently confirmed BYTE-IDENTICAL by collate.py, fully supporting the row's claim that the deceit/falsehood clause recurs. But two warrant-language defects survive re-derivation from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings (see challenges): the rejected_alternative's 'no addressee or mode shift' claim is factually wrong and self-contradicts the row's own rationale, and the 'byte-checked, word order recurs unchanged' claim overstates the collation tier for two of three recurring fragments. Neither defect overturns the span choice itself - v11's imperative genuinely does function as an echo/frame of 7-8 rather than fresh material - but the stated warrant needs repair, which is why this is filed as a challenge on the warrant rather than the span. The medium (not high) confidence the row already carries is, on this evidence, well calibrated.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative's claim that 'no addressee or mode shift separates' vv144.9-11 is factually inaccurate and self-contradicts the row's own rationale, which elsewhere correctly treats v144.11 as reopening imperative petition material distinct from v144.9's vow and v144.10's declarative predicate.
challenges.evidence: Pointed bytes spliced from verse_map_oshb.json (never hand-typed): v144.9's verb is the 1cs cohortative אָשִׁ֣ירָה ('I will sing' - vow mode); v144.10 opens with the participial predicate הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן ('[you are] he who gives' - declarative-descriptive mode); v144.11 opens with the paired 2ms imperatives פְּצֵ֥נִי וְהַצִּילֵנִי֮ ('rescue me, and deliver me' - imperative-petition mode), the same imperative register that opens v144.5's own theophany petition. Three distinct grammatical moods across vv9-11, not zero as claimed. The row's own rationale field independently corroborates this by calling v144.11 a reopening of 'the rescue plea' with 'paired imperatives' - language that only makes sense if v144.11 IS a mode shift from the vow/declarative material immediately before it.

challenges.claim: The row's 'byte-checked, the word order recurs unchanged across web:Ps.144.7 and web:Ps.144.11' claim names no tier and overstates byte-grade fidelity for two of the three recurring fragments, which independently collate at accent_stripped and skeleton tiers respectively, not byte tier.
challenges.evidence: collate.py tier results (batch run against verse_map_oshb.json): the rescue-plea bigram v144.7's פְּצֵ֣נִי וְ֭הַצִּילֵנִי vs v144.11's פְּצֵ֥נִי וְהַצִּילֵנִי֮ collates at tier=accent_stripped (cantillation differs); the foreigners phrase v144.7's מִ֝יַּ֗ד בְּנֵ֣י נֵכָֽר vs v144.11's מִיַּ֪ד בְּֽנֵי נֵ֫כָ֥ר collates at tier=skeleton (vowel pointing differs, not only cantillation); only the deceit/falsehood clause - v144.8 in full vs v144.11's tail אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּ֭יהֶם דִּבֶּר שָׁ֑וְא וִֽ֝ימִינָ֗ם יְמִ֣ין שָֽׁקֶר - collates at tier=byte. Per the campaign's TIER/ORDINAL DISCIPLINE standing rule, 'byte-identical'-adjacent language needs the tier named per fragment; here one fragment is byte, one is accent_stripped, one is skeleton, and the row's phrasing does not distinguish them.

reviews.reasoning: Span 12-15 unfolds the prosperity vision (12-14, opened by a purpose/relative clause continuing the petition just closed) and closes on the psalm's doubled beatitude (15), the parent's own final verse - a clean capstone with no rival seam nearby (check_tiling.py confirms the cluster's 4 rows tile Ps 144's 15 WEB verses exactly, no gaps or overlaps; check_refs_mirror.py and citation_sweep.py both run GREEN on this row). All Hebrew quotes in this row collate at byte tier. One citation-format defect survives (below): observed_substrate_signals[1] quotes verbatim WEB text in single curly quotes rather than the book-wide double-curly convention, which independently reproduces as a check_web_quotes.py delimiter-evasion flag. This is a register/citation-format defect, not a boundary or factual error - the span and warrant otherwise hold and the high confidence rating is not undermined by it.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[1] quotes the verbatim WEB phrase 'Happy are the people' in single curly quotes instead of the book-wide-mandated double curly quotes for WEB text, a QUOTE CONVENTION violation (OL-c13/OL-c20) that evades check_web_quotes.py's verbatim validator.
challenges.evidence: Independent run of check_web_quotes.py against the cluster rows reproduces the defect mechanically: flags=[{"path": "[3].observed_substrate_signals[1]", "quote": "Happy are the people", "issue": "verbatim WEB text in SINGLE curly quotes (delimiter evasion - rows use double curly + inline web: ref)"}]. TOOLKIT.md's book-wide QUOTE CONVENTION (OL-c13/OL-c20) reserves double curly quotes for WEB text; the source verse (web:Ps.144.15, verse_map_web.json) reads 'Happy are the people who are in such a situation. Happy are the people whose God is Yahweh.' - the quoted fragment is genuine verbatim WEB text and belongs in double curly quotes with its existing inline web:Ps.144.15 ref.
